subject.title: feat: add linux/riscv64 Docker image to multi-platform build

question: Should OpenClaw add linux/riscv64 as an official Docker release platform now, and should failure remain non-blocking for the existing amd64/arm64 release contract?
rationale: This expands official release infrastructure and support expectations rather than fixing a broken existing contract, so maintainers need to own the platform, validation, and operator-impact policy before implementation.

options.title: Add non-blocking riscv64 images
options.body: Build riscv64 with QEMU, publish its digest only when successful, and require live release-path proof before treating the platform as official.

options.title: Defer official riscv64 Docker support
options.body: Keep this open or close by maintainer decision until release capacity, dependency support, and adjacent runtime behavior are ready.

options.title: Use an experimental separate image path
options.body: Publish riscv64 outside the main multi-arch manifest until maintainers are comfortable with reliability and support guarantees.

recommendation.title: Add non-blocking riscv64 images
recommendation.body: Build riscv64 with QEMU, publish its digest only when successful, and require live release-path proof before treating the platform as official.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Docker release, attestation, and official Docker docs history makes this the best available routing owner for the product/ops choice.
